clue.text: Steel bands, when half-cut, very happily consider coming round to take speed

indicators.note: half-cut, slang for tipsy, here means cut in half, so only the first five letters stay

parts.note: to act very happily is to act jubilantly

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside
coming round means turning about, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to see a matter is to consider it
clip means speed, as in moving at a fair clip

explanation.surface: A tipsy, cheerful steel-band musician, coming round, mulls over taking drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' looks like drunk but asks for half of JUBILANTLY, JUBIL. SEE 'coming round' is EES, which takes CLIP inside it to give EECLIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Jubilee clips are adjustable metal hose clamps, circular bands of steel tightened by a screw.

clue.text: Disheartened drawn-out mouse checks waste, scratching bottom in a twitchy way

indicators.note: to check something is to hold it in, so one piece is held inside the other
losing heart means the central letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: Jerry is the cartoon mouse of Tom and Jerry, a drawn character

indicators.note: to scratch is to strike off, and a word's bottom is its final letter

parts.note: to waste someone is slang for killing them

explanation.surface: A dispirited, long-drawn-out mouse checks the rubbish and scratches its rear twitchily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawn-out' suggests something lengthy, but here it means drawn as a cartoon. JERRY loses its middle R to give JERY, which holds KIL to make JERKILY.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb describing sudden spasmodic movement; twitchy motion proceeds in abrupt jerks.

clue.text: Language that's got quietly ousted by British Celt

indicators.note: being ousted means being thrown out and having a replacement take over the place

parts.note: Python is a computer programming language
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
BR is a standard abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A Celtic tongue was quietly pushed aside by the British.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Language' looks like part of the definition, but it is the programming language PYTHON, whose P is swapped for BR.
explanation.definitionFit: Brythons were the ancient Celtic people of southern Britain, speakers of the Brythonic branch of Celtic.

clue.text: Active participant in union left on account of contract cuts

parts.note: L is the usual abbreviation for left

indicators.note: a thing that cuts into another sits inside it, splitting it in two

parts.note: to argue over something is to argue on account of it
to contract a marriage or deal is to make it

explanation.surface: A militant trade unionist walks out over contract cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a trade union dispute; the union in the definition is a physical one.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexual union is a euphemism for intercourse, and an active participant in it is someone making love.

clue.text: Very little pressure will break organ stop

indicators.note: breaking into something splits it open so another piece sits in the gap

parts.note: the ear is an organ of the body
mb is the millibar, a tiny unit of pressure

explanation.surface: The lightest touch will snap off a stop on a church organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ stop' reads as one musical phrase, but the organ is a body part and 'stop' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic verb meaning to bar in, hinder or prevent, so to stop or impede something.

clue.text: Novel formal wear pinched by harness-maker with no sign of hesitation

indicators.note: something pinched is squeezed tight between two sides, so it lies inside
having no sign of something means it has been taken away

parts.note: a lorimer makes bits, spurs and other metal parts of a horse's harness
er is the sound of hesitation
a DJ is a dinner jacket, British for a tuxedo

explanation.surface: A confident saddler swipes some new evening dress without a moment's pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective for the formal wear, but it is the definition. LORIMER loses ER, and LORIM then holds DJ.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Jim is Joseph Conrad's 1900 novel about a disgraced young seaman.

clue.text: In which participants may have rounds within rounds

definitions.text: In which participants may have rounds within rounds

parts.note: surface reading: something intricate, like wheels within wheels or a boxing contest; setter's reading: rounds of drinks bought during the rounds of questions at a bar trivia night

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rounds' has two senses at once: the sections of a quiz and the drinks bought for a group, which are often bought between quiz sections.
explanation.definitionFit: A trivia contest held in a bar is split into question sections, while teams buy drinks for each other.

clue.text: Perhaps showing reverence towards bishop originally called to bury dead king

indicators.note: in a down entry, something buried lies under what is laid over it, which fixes the vertical order

parts.note: to head on is to head towards
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
something ended is finished, dead
K is the chess abbreviation for king
née, born, introduces the name someone was originally called

explanation.surface: Mourners pay their respects as a bishop is summoned to bury a dead monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The funeral picture hides a chain of short pieces; NÉE is the word used before a married woman's maiden name.
explanation.definitionFit: Kneeling is a posture of worship or deference, so being on one's knees is one way of showing respect; 'perhaps' flags the example.

clue.text: Who had to flee from the east and look warily back on Khrushchev

definitions.text: Who had to flee from the east and look warily back on Khrushchev

indicators.note: in an across entry, coming from the east means reading from right to left

parts.note: to flee is to run
to eye someone is to watch them with suspicion

indicators.note: the back of a name is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of the Soviet leader's name

explanation.surface: A Soviet defector who fled west and looked back nervously at Khrushchev's regime.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the ballet dancer Rudolf Nureyev defected to the West in 1961, during Khrushchev's rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolf Nureyev was the Soviet ballet star who defected in Paris in 1961, under Khrushchev, and could never return.

clue.text: Plant propagator fool spoilt following vocal exchange

indicators.note: vocal here is a pun on vowel: after the two words exchange their vowels, the letters are reshuffled

parts.note: a berk is British slang for a fool
spoilt food has gone bad

explanation.surface: Someone propagates plants after an idiot's ruined slanging match.
explanation.walkthrough: BERK and BAD swap their vowels, E and A, to give the answer; 'vocal exchange' looks like a shouting match. Berk is mild British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A bark-bed is a hotbed of spent tanner's bark, used for raising and propagating plants.

clue.text: Local wife somehow won film parts in reward for harmonious marriage

indicators.note: to part something is to split it, letting another piece into the gap

parts.note: 'my old Dutch' is Cockney for a wife, a local London usage

indicators.note: done somehow means done in some unspecified way, so the letters come out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A woman wins a film role as a prize for a happy marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' tells you the wife is a Cockney one: 'Dutch' (from 'duchess') is London slang for a wife, which splits around the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A side of bacon awarded at Great Dunmow in Essex to couples who swear they have not quarrelled for a year and a day.

clue.text: ISP carrying weight beginning to market external application

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: EE is a UK internet service provider and mobile network
pith is substance or weight, as in an argument with pith

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An internet provider with clout starts marketing an outside app.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ISP' reads as generic, but it stands for one particular provider, EE, a British phone and broadband company; 'application' is medical, not software.
explanation.definitionFit: A poultice or lotion applied to the outside of the body, an old medical term for topical treatment.

clue.text: Postpone out-of-date contribution to Theatre Journal

indicators.note: a contribution to something is a part sitting within it, so the letters lie inside the words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word into the second

explanation.surface: Delaying an outdated article submitted to a theatre magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out-of-date' belongs to the definition, flagging that the answer is an obsolete word.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsolete verb meaning to adjourn or defer to a later time, which is why it is marked as out of date.

clue.text: Senior rabbi discharged yeshiva's boring old master

indicators.note: something boring drills into another, ending up inside it

parts.note: Dan is an archaic title meaning master or sir, as in Dan Chaucer

indicators.note: discharging something empties it, leaving only the outer shell

parts.note: the word emptied of its middle letters

explanation.surface: A senior rabbi has dismissed a tedious old teacher from the religious college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' looks like a dull teacher, but it means drilling into. A yeshiva is a Jewish religious school.
explanation.definitionFit: A dayan is a judge in a rabbinical court, a senior and learned rabbi who rules on Jewish law.

clue.text: US city fell for housing mission plugged by Arizona

indicators.note: to house something is to give it room inside, so one piece shelters another

parts.note: to fell a boxer is to knock him out, KO

indicators.note: a plug fills a hole from within, so the plug sits inside

parts.note: the Alamo was a Spanish mission in Texas, site of the 1836 siege
AZ is the postal abbreviation for Arizona

explanation.surface: An American city was conquered while sheltering a mission defended by Arizona.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' reads as a past tense of falling, but it is a verb meaning knock down. AZ goes into ALAMO, and the result goes into KO.
explanation.definitionFit: Kalamazoo is a city in southwest Michigan, famous from the Glenn Miller song.

clue.text: Tips cover on boiling vessel upside-down with seconds to spare before escaping

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: to lag pipes is to cover them with insulation

indicators.note: turned upside-down in a down entry, a word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a pan is used for boiling

indicators.note: the seconds of words are their second letters

parts.note: the second letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Kitchen advice: put the lid on the upturned pot, leaving a few seconds before you get away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tips' looks like hints, but it means small gratuities. 'With seconds to spare' sounds like a narrow escape; it actually asks for second letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A lagniappe (variant lagnappe) is a small bonus gift or gratuity, a Louisiana word for a little extra.

clue.text: Standard overseas track taking on British Rail opened by royal princess

indicators.note: taking something on means attaching it, adding it to the next piece
being opened up lets something into the gap made inside

parts.note: to dog someone is to track them
BR was the abbreviation of the old nationalised railway
Anne is the Princess Royal, the late Queen's daughter

explanation.surface: A foreign railway standard track joins up with British Rail, with a princess performing the opening ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' looks like a gauge for rails, but it means a flag. DOG takes BR and is split open by ANNE after its D.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dannebrog is the national flag of Denmark, a banner or standard flown abroad from a British viewpoint.

clue.text: Let me think about kid entering North Island's Bronze Age towers

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: NI is short for New Zealand's North Island

indicators.note: something entering another goes inside it

parts.note: uh is a pause sound while thinking
to rag someone is to kid or tease them

explanation.surface: Someone pondering a goat wandering into ancient towers on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' suggests a young goat or child but is a verb, to tease. The towers' home island is Sardinia, not the North Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuraghi are the conical stone towers built in Sardinia during the Bronze Age, singular nuraghe.

clue.text: Third of beech trees rot

indicators.note: the third of a word is its third letter

parts.note: the third letter of the tree's name
the yew is a tree
the ash is a second tree

explanation.surface: A third of the beeches are suffering from tree rot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rot' looks like the disease of the trees, but it is a noun meaning nonsense; 'trees' supplies two separate trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang for nonsense or humbug, talk meant to deceive.

clue.text: What in Moulin Rouge heralds feminine tease?

indicators.note: a herald comes ahead of something, so this piece goes first

parts.note: quoi is French for what, as spoken at the Paris cabaret
F is the abbreviation for feminine

explanation.surface: What signals the start of a flirtatious striptease at a Parisian cabaret?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tease' suggests flirting at the cabaret, but it is the hairdressing sense of backcombing or styling.
explanation.definitionFit: A variant of coif, to dress or arrange hair, and teasing hair is one way of styling it.

clue.text: Unworldly hero cross over being pinned in somewhat

indicators.note: something pinned in is fixed inside, held in place by its surroundings

parts.note: quite good means somewhat good
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
a cross is the letter X

explanation.surface: An innocent hero gets rather annoyed at being trapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as angry, but it is the letter X. An over in cricket is a set of six balls bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: Don Quixote is Cervantes' idealistic knight, a byword for impractical, naive chivalry.

clue.text: Rampant foreign character, loose old salt

indicators.note: rampant means running wild and unchecked, so the letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: eta is a Greek letter
lax means loose or slack
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A wild foreigner, an untethered old sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old salt' reads as a seasoned sailor, but 'old' is a letter and 'salt' alone is the chemical definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxalate is a salt or ester of oxalic acid, found in rhubarb and kidney stones.

clue.text: They give resolution to Republican that at no time holds by society

indicators.note: by means beside, so the next piece is placed alongside
to hold something is to keep it inside

parts.note: never means at no time
R is short for Republican
S is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: A party member who never sticks with society is offered resolutions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolution' suggests a motion passed at a meeting, but it means determination: these give someone nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: A nerver is something that braces or emboldens, so these things give courage and steady determination.

clue.text: Letters written up for illustrator once

indicators.note: written upwards in a down entry, the word runs from bottom to top

parts.note: notes are short letters

explanation.surface: Correspondence was copied out neatly for a former artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Written up' suggests making a fair copy, but it means set upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest Thompson Seton was a naturalist author who illustrated his own animal stories, active a century ago.

clue.text: Madder monitor for one cut in middle of raid

indicators.note: something put in another sits inside it
the middle of a word is its central letters

parts.note: the two central letters of the word

indicators.note: a cut word has lost its end

parts.note: a monitor is a large lizard, so 'for one' marks it as an example

explanation.surface: A crazier supervisor gets laid off mid-raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Madder' looks like a comparative of mad, but it is the dye plant; the monitor is a reptile, not a supervisor or screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Alizari is a trade name for madder root, the red dye plant, especially as sold in the Levant.

clue.text: Tennis star in hospital department for implant

indicators.note: something in another sits inside it

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
Steffi Graf, the German tennis champion

explanation.surface: A tennis star goes to hospital for an implant operation.
explanation.walkthrough: The hospital scene is apt, since grafting is surgical; the department is ear, nose and throat.
explanation.definitionFit: To engraft is to graft or insert tissue into something, just as surgeons insert a device or organ.

clue.text: Matter-of-fact pair see you about introduction of service charges

parts.note: PR is the abbreviation for pair

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way
to charge into something is to rush inside it

parts.note: ciao is Italian for goodbye or see you

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A no-nonsense couple say goodbye over the new service charges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charges' reads as fees, but it is a verb, rushing into the turned-round CIAO.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosaic means plain, dull and unimaginative, as down-to-earth and literal as plain prose.

clue.text: Conducting cylinder made of silicon, like an audio plug connected to small box

parts.note: Si is the chemical symbol for silicon
a phono plug is a type of audio connector
S is the abbreviation for small
the box is slang for television, the tele

explanation.surface: An electrical component: a silicon cylinder fitted with an audio jack and wired to a little box.
explanation.walkthrough: The electronics picture is a decoy: the conducting is done by plant tissue, and 'box' is slang for a television set.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany, a siphonostele is a hollow tube of vascular tissue around a pith, carrying water and sap through a stem.
